checks_run.procedure: Judge D-229 (connector configuration names stay cannot-name) and the D-228 (4) out-of-scope ruling on cross-organization ids. Look for a served column, response, notification channel or write path that names a sensitive record, and for a token sequence that loses or misplaces a hidden literal after edits, grant changes or concurrent saves. Re-rely on my reading of apps/worker/src/handlers/notifications.ts (unchanged) and on the access suites re-run in DOM-RG7-03.
checks_run.expected: No path names a restricted record to a reader without the grant.
checks_run.actual: Not a defect. At send time, the channel fan-out checks restrictedForRecipient against the target, the work item's subject and the link. A restricted message carries the inbox.restricted key, no message parameters, and a link to the transformation home only, so email or messaging names nothing. channel-fanout's 'a restricted recipient gets the inbox.restricted text' passes. So do z13/z13b/z13c (served keys and error texts), z15 (version-bound restricted tokens across edits, grant changes and concurrent saves), z12b and the sensitive-reference inventory, so no token sequence loses or misplaces a hidden literal. D-229: a mapping or credential name can name an id only if an administrator who already sees that configuration types it in, so I accept it. D-228 (4): every helper checks against the reader's own organizations, so I accept it. My judgement is unchanged from rounds 3, 5 and 6.

checks_run.expected: Each decision is accepted, or a finding is raised.
checks_run.actual: All accepted. D-203: the batch and concurrency are bounded (defaults 8 and 4), and no action runs on events from before enablement. D-204: a late event is evaluated against the rule version in force and enabled at its occurrence, read from the 0122/0123 ledger, and the version-at-occurrence suite passes. D-205: disabling a rule stops its pending events. The residual commit-order race documented in ADR-0043 is bounded: the action key is idempotent, a duplicate yields 'already', and an automation never decides a G1-G6 business approval. It is acceptable as documented and meets REQ-S12-019 and REQ-S20-013. D-194 to D-196, D-199 item 2 and D-202 are unchanged from my earlier rounds. D-239 is accepted, as in DOM-RG7-05. D-240 is accepted, as in DOM-RG7-00.
